LESSON: SONGS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.3: Songs

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Songs. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What does good singing involve?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. sing different types of songs applying performance techniques
2. perform the East African Community Anthem in unison
3. identify types of folk songs performed by indigenous Kenyan communities
4. perform an indigenous Kenyan folk song applying performance techniques
5. value performing indigenous songs from different Kenyan communities

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SONGS
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Songs helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: SONGS
Study Songs like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Sing different types of songs applying performance techniques

What this means
In this part you learn to sing different types of songs applying performance techniques. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: sing different types of songs applying performance techniques.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Songs” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can sing different types of songs applying performance techniques. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Perform the East African Community Anthem in unison

What this means
In this part you learn to perform the East African Community Anthem in unison. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform the East African Community Anthem in unison.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Songs in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform the East African Community Anthem in unison. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Identify types of folk songs performed by indigenous Kenyan communities

What this means
In this part you learn to identify types of folk songs performed by indigenous Kenyan communities. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify types of folk songs performed by indigenous Kenyan communities.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify types of folk songs performed by indigenous Kenyan communities. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Perform an indigenous Kenyan folk song applying performance techniques

What this means
In this part you learn to perform an indigenous Kenyan folk song applying performance techniques. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform an indigenous Kenyan folk song applying performance techniques.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Songs” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform an indigenous Kenyan folk song applying performance techniques. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Value performing indigenous songs from different Kenyan communities

What this means
In this part you learn to value performing indigenous songs from different Kenyan communities. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value performing indigenous songs from different Kenyan communities.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Songs in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value performing indigenous songs from different Kenyan communities. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Songs is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Songs” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: sing different types of songs applying performance techniques)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Songs in your own words. (skill: perform the East African Community Anthem in unison)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: identify types of folk songs performed by indigenous Kenyan communities)

Example 4: Show how “Songs” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: perform an indigenous Kenyan folk song applying performance techniques)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Songs to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: sing different types of songs applying performance techniques.
3. Practise this skill: perform the East African Community Anthem in unison.
4. Practise this skill: identify types of folk songs performed by indigenous Kenyan communities.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Songs from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Songs: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Songs?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What does good singing involve?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Songs means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: sing different types of songs applying performance techniques.
5. Be able to: perform the East African Community Anthem in unison.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
